Subject: Request for custom uptime+latency commitment for strategic deployment

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our product team at HydroCore is putting Redwood into the critical path for our image-tagging pipeline, and leadership is asking for a stronger service commitment than your standard offering. High-level ask: a written commitment for 99.995% monthly uptime and 50ms p50 inference latency (multi-region: us-west + us-east + eu-west fallback).

We understand this is outside of standard SLAs, so we are open to a structured carveout (higher reserved capacity, committed spend, technical constraints). Attached is a short requirements doc and our expected traffic profile for peak/steady load. Can you send a proposed exception runbook and a timeline for approvals? Procurement is on the thread — we need this agreed before end of June to make our launch.

Ava Collins

Folks — quick feasibility summary attached (sre_capacity_estimate.csv). TL;DR: 50ms p50 is feasible for 90% of HydroCore's planned inference profile if we provision:

- Dedicated reserved capacity across two active regions (us-west + us-east) with a third region (eu-west) as geo-failover.
- Continuous small-batch pre-warming of model workers to avoid KV cold-starts; this increases baseline GPU-hours by ~28%.
- A minimum burst pool (hot reserve) for 7x intra-minute spikes and a static routing policy that pins HydroCore traffic to reserved nodes.

Risks and notes:
- Cross-region p50 will vary; inter-region network adds ~8-12ms median on top of inference. Guarantee needs to be scoped to single-region p50 where traffic is pinned.
- 99.995% monthly uptime is aggressive — requires full redundancy (N+2) per region and faster incident RCA/mitigation playbooks.
- We can offer a contractual SLA that ties the 99.995% to the reserved capacity profile (committed spend), with defined excluded windows (plumbing, customer misconfiguration, force majeure).

Cost estimate: attached; commercial to confirm discounting.

—Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sre_capacity_estimate.csv
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for custom uptime+latency commitment for strategic deployment

Thanks Monica — thorough. A few legal/practical guardrails:

- We can draft a custom SLA but require the commitment to be tied to explicit operational prerequisites: committed monthly spend (term 12mo+), named contact for incident ops, and a mutually agreed runbook with documented failover testing cadence.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows, customer-side network issues, and third-party infra (cloud provider outages). We should also add a ‘grace period’ for the first 30 days post-launch to allow tuning; SLA only applies after launch acceptance test.
- Credits: propose a tiered credit table but cap max credits at 50% of monthly committed fees.

Approvals: VP Eng (Vivek) sign-off required for any SLA that includes availability >99.99% and/or any uptime credit exposure above standard tiers. Finance will need approval on discounting.

I'll draft redlines and a short approval memo once we have the SRE cost inputs.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for custom uptime+latency commitment for strategic deployment

Quick product note: two technical items to flag that affect the commitment runbook:

1) Model variants + quantization: If HydroCore wants the absolute p50 across all model variants (quantized + fp16), we need to pin a tested variant and lock model upgrades behind a maintenance window; automatic model upgrades could change latency. Suggest we require a change-control process for model rollouts for this account.

2) KV cache warm state: The routing policy should prefer sticky sessions or pinned keys where possible for production traffic. If HydroCore's workload includes many cold prefixes, p50 will be higher than our projection.

I'll draft the product constraints section for the runbook.

—Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
